result.scientific_strategy:
## c92ccfe2-1135-4ec4-bc5a-eded729fc461 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes on the unchanged full-range reach-and-hold task. The strongest saved policy, checkpoint-100352 (working and best-known), succeeds on 1945/2000 = 97.25% of two disjoint 1000-episode full-range panels (97.2% seed 6000, 97.3% seed 8000), 99.5% on the reused seed-5000 selection panel and 98.0% on the reused task-reference panel. The deficit is not radial: every 6-20 cm radius band sits at 96.8-97.6%, while angle bins from -120 degrees to +180 degrees are 98-100% and the lower-left quadrant carries nearly all failures: [-150,-120) 72.9% (46/170) and [-180,-150) 96.6% (6/177). Failures are marginal in magnitude - 28 of 55 never enter the 1 cm tolerance (25 stopping 1.0-1.5 cm short) and 27 enter but hold fewer than 50 of the 100 required steps. The deficit therefore sits inside the trained 14-20 cm distribution, concentrated in a roughly 40-degree angular band. The 50% lower-left curriculum experiment was measured on a disjoint shared panel and produced 96.4% at its early measured checkpoint and 91.8% at its final checkpoint, below the 97.2% working policy, with additional positive-angle and near-target regressions. The lower-left joint-limit/IK-branch explanation remains a code-inspection hypothesis, not a measured mechanism.

**Lessons and limits:** The 14-20 cm training annulus was not the binding gap: near targets (6-14 cm) generalize at about 97.6%, no worse than the trained bands, and the deficit is in-distribution. Extended training of the same recipe gave no measured gain - checkpoint-100352 beats the later checkpoint-120832 on a shared 1000-episode panel (97.2% vs 96.2%) and on every paired comparison (12-1 over 1200 episodes), with checkpoint-115712 (96.7%, 7-1) and checkpoint-105472 (96.7%, 6-0) also behind. The training proxy plateaued at 0.93-0.97 after about 94,208 steps while measured failures stayed angularly structured, and the proxy peak of the curriculum challenger did not predict task success. The baseline already oversampled -165 to -115 degrees at 25%; increasing that probability to 50% did not repair the sector and disturbed other sectors, so coverage alone is not established as the binding remedy. The reward currently gives no forfeiture for leaving tolerance after accumulating hold progress, making hold stability a distinct, measurable training signal; this is a plausible intervention, not evidence that reward is the cause. Transfer from checkpoint-100352 preserves the learned observation/action semantics and broad reach-and-hold behavior, whereas a representation change would require a fresh semantic contract. Limits: the two 1000-episode panels that drive the 97.25% estimate were also used to rank checkpoints, so they carry selection context; the 98.0% task-reference figure reuses one fixed 200-episode panel and is not independent confirmation. The angular decomposition is descriptive. The link between the lower-left deficit and shoulder-limit/IK-branch geometry is a code-inspection hypothesis, not a measured property of the policy. The attempted experiment-2 record is invalid and unmeasured, so its 50% curriculum change cannot be treated as a negative or positive result.

**Open questions:** Can explicit cost for interrupting an accumulated hold improve the 100-step completion rate, particularly among lower-left episodes that already enter tolerance, without sacrificing the broad-distribution reach behavior? Is the remaining never-enter deficit a training-optimization artifact or a stable consequence of the joint-limit and IK-reference geometry? Would a representation or target-distribution change address that deficit without disturbing the near-perfect sectors? How variable is the learning process under the unchanged baseline recipe, and can hold-boundary oscillation recur under altered training conditions? These uncertainties remain open and are not a prescribed experiment queue.
